newsitem.title: USA: Company to make earrings from Diana's gown.
newsitem.headline: Company to make earrings from Diana's gown.

text.p: A company that bought one of Princess Diana's gowns at auction plans to snip off its thousands of beads and fake pearls and sell them as earrings.

The earrings will be priced at $1,000 a pair and the proceeds will go to charity, Arnold Duke, an owner of Rockville, Maryland-based International Gem, Mineral and Jewelry Show Inc., said on Wednesday.
His sister Roxanne Duke bought the dress for $34,500 at the Christie's auction last month in New York. The sale of 79 of Diana's gowns reaped more than $3.2 million for charity.
The Dukes have defended their plan against criticism that they are destroying the dress by designer Catherine Walker.
"So many people wanted to buy a dress that belonged to Diana and couldn't afford it," Roxanne Duke said. "This way they can own something that she wore."
She said the fake pearls could be removed without destroying the dress. She also said the company may replace the fake pearls and beads that are removed.
The dress has about 20,000 fake pearls and beads. The Dukes said they were still in the process of choosing a designer for the earrings and charities for the proceeds.
A few people have already reserved a pair of the earrings, Arnold Duke said.
